Total protein content (Abrin) reduced by ~36.5-44.7%, maximum in Kanji-Shodhita samples, indicating significant removal of toxic protein.
Total protein content decreased by 96.59–99.78% after Shodhana, with the greatest reduction in Kanji-treated samples, indicating marked reduction of the toxic protein (abrin)

Both groups receiving 500 mg/day Shilajit for 21 days showed a significant reduction in blood glucose levels in newly diagnosed hyperglycemic subjects, indicating effective hypoglycemic activity for both purification methods.
Overall alkaloid content reduced in processed samples (A > B > C > D), supporting chemical detoxification.

Shodhita Bhanga significantly reduced pain (84.1%), anxiety, and depression, improved quality of life, and showed no major adverse effects, dependency, or withdrawal symptoms. In contrast, unprocessed Cannabis is associated with habit formation and cognitive impairment, indicating that Shodhana improves its safety and therapeutic efficacy.
Processed samples (especially milk-treated) significantly prolonged sleeping time without convulsions, showing reduced toxicity and enhanced CNS depressant activity.
Processed samples reduced locomotor activity in a controlled manner at sub-convulsive doses, indicating safer CNS depressant action.
Crude drug hastened convulsions (4.75 min), whereas processed samples significantly delayed onset (up to 11.25 min in milk-treated), demonstrating anticonvulsant transformation.
Diazepam completely prevented lethality of processed samples at LD₁₀₀ doses, confirming manageable and reduced neurotoxicity after Shodhana.
Processed samples antagonized morphine-induced catalepsy while crude potentiated it, indicating beneficial neuropharmacological modification.
Shodhana produced an ~70% reduction in total alkaloid content in both Datura metel and Datura innoxia, confirming effective detoxification.

Shankha Bhasma purified with lemon juice showed significantly higher symptom resolution (66 to 71% vs. 27 to 31%, P < 0.005) and more heartburn-free days, confirming improved therapeutic efficacy after proper Shodhana.
Absence of red colour in spent purification media (appearing only after acid digestion) confirms ferric ions were removed as chelated complexes, proving detoxification.
Toxic metals (As, Cd, Hg, Pb) remained within permissible limits in Badrashma Pishti, confirming safety for therapeutic use.
Anacardol increased from 47.51% to 50.62% after Shodhana, suggesting decarboxylation of toxic anacardic acid into the less toxic anacardol, thereby supporting detoxification.
Reduced from 35.40% to 28.71% w/w, suggesting removal of irritant oil constituents during Shodhana.

THC ( Delta 9-tetrahydrocannabinol) content decreased by 26–85% after Shodhana, depending on the purification method, confirming significant removal of the narcotic principle. The greatest reduction (85%) was achieved by washing the leaves until free from turbidity followed by frying in ghee, indicating this as the most effective detoxification method.
Toxic albumins and globulins were present before Shodhana but absent after Shodhana, confirming detoxification.

Protein content of the seeds decreased from 8.73% to 6.51%, while the protein content of the Shodhana milk increased from 4.76% to 7.99%, indicating the transfer of proteinaceous toxic constituents (including abrin) from the seeds into the processing medium during Shodhana.

Microscopic analysis showed that Shodhana reduced glandular trichomes (the major site of tetrahydrocannabinol, THC, accumulation), along with fragmented fibers, reduced cystoliths, and shrunken/distorted epidermal cells, indicating structural modifications associated with reduced psychoactive THC content and detoxification.
No treatment-related toxicity or adverse clinical effects were observed at therapeutic or higher doses, confirming good long-term safety.
Overall toxicity assessment showed that Tuttha Bhasma was well tolerated at the therapeutic dose, with no dose-dependent toxicity, confirming the safety of the properly prepared Bhasma.

Purified Bhallataka exhibited greater thrombolytic activity (66.59% clot lysis) than raw Bhallataka (59.82%), demonstrating that Shodhana enhances the thrombolytic efficacy while producing a safer form of the drug.
XRPD confirmed transformation of raw coral and demonstrated reduced crystallite/particle size after repeated grinding and calcination, indicating structural modification during Marana.

XRPD showed complete transformation of calcium carbonate from the aragonite phase in raw Mukta Shukti to the more stable calcite phase in Mukta Shukti Bhasma, with minor portlandite [Ca(OH)₂] formation.

ICP-MS analysis showed that Shodhana markedly reduced silver (5138 to 119.5 ppm), copper (2866.1 to 0.5324 ppm), and tin (0.371 to 0.3233 ppm) impurities, producing purified mercury with elemental composition closer to commercially available mercury.
Chemical analysis showed an increase in sulfur content from 89.39% to 97.14% after Shodhana, confirming improved purity of Sulphur.
Amino acid content was reduced after Shodhana, with no detectable amino acids in the distilled water-treated Guñjā samples, confirming depletion of proteinaceous constituents.
Strychnine and brucine were detected in the post-Shodhana milk, confirming removal of the principal toxic alkaloids from Nux-vomica seeds during Shodhana.
